question: For whose good is the choice of rulers?

window_text.1: Abimelek son of Jerub-Baal went to his mother’s brothers in Shechem and said to them and to all his mother’s clan,
window_text.2: “Ask all the citizens of Shechem, ‘Which is better for you: to have all seventy of Jerub-Baal’s sons rule over you, or just one man?’ Remember, I am your flesh and blood.”

question: Who says Abimelek is their relative?

window_text.3: When the brothers repeated all this to the citizens of Shechem, they were inclined to follow Abimelek, for they said, “He is related to us.”
window_text.4: They gave him seventy shekels of silver from the temple of Baal-Berith, and Abimelek used it to hire reckless scoundrels, who became his followers.
window_text.5: He went to his father’s home in Ophrah and on one stone murdered his seventy brothers, the sons of Jerub-Baal. But Jotham, the youngest son of Jerub-Baal, escaped by hiding.
window_text.6: Then all the citizens of Shechem and Beth Millo gathered beside the great tree at the pillar in Shechem to crown Abimelek king.

question: For what purpose would the olive tree give up its oil?

window_text.9: “But the olive tree answered, ‘Should I give up my oil, by which both gods and humans are honored, to hold sway over the trees?’
window_text.10: “Next, the trees said to the fig tree, ‘Come and be our king.’

question: Whom do all the trees finally ask to be king?

window_text.13: “But the vine answered, ‘Should I give up my wine, which cheers both gods and humans, to hold sway over the trees?’
window_text.14: “Finally all the trees said to the thornbush, ‘Come and be our king.’

question: What happens if the trees do not accept the thornbush as king?
answer: Fire comes from the thornbush and burns the cedars of Lebanon.
competitor: The trees come to find shade under the thornbush.

window_text.15: “The thornbush said to the trees, ‘If you really want to anoint me king over you, come and take refuge in my shade; but if not, then let fire come out of the thornbush and consume the cedars of Lebanon!’
window_text.16: “Have you acted honorably and in good faith by making Abimelek king? Have you been fair to Jerub-Baal and his family? Have you treated him as he deserves?
window_text.17: Remember that my father fought for you and risked his life to rescue you from the hand of Midian.

question: What is called down if the citizens have not acted rightly toward Jerub-Baal?
answer: Fire between Abimelek and the citizens, each destroying the other.
competitor: Mutual joy between Abimelek and the citizens.

window_text.18: But today you have revolted against my father’s family. You have murdered his seventy sons on a single stone and have made Abimelek, the son of his female slave, king over the citizens of Shechem because he is related to you.
window_text.19: So have you acted honorably and in good faith toward Jerub-Baal and his family today? If you have, may Abimelek be your joy, and may you be his, too!
window_text.20: But if you have not, let fire come out from Abimelek and consume you, the citizens of Shechem and Beth Millo, and let fire come out from you, the citizens of Shechem and Beth Millo, and consume Abimelek!”

window_text.21: Then Jotham fled, escaping to Beer, and he lived there because he was afraid of his brother Abimelek.
window_text.22: After Abimelek had governed Israel three years,
window_text.23: God stirred up animosity between Abimelek and the citizens of Shechem so that they acted treacherously against Abimelek.
window_text.24: God did this in order that the crime against Jerub-Baal’s seventy sons, the shedding of their blood, might be avenged on their brother Abimelek and on the citizens of Shechem, who had helped him murder his brothers.
window_text.25: In opposition to him these citizens of Shechem set men on the hilltops to ambush and rob everyone who passed by, and this was reported to Abimelek.

question: Who had gained the citizens’ trust by the time they cursed Abimelek at the festival?

window_text.26: Now Gaal son of Ebed moved with his clan into Shechem, and its citizens put their confidence in him.
window_text.27: After they had gone out into the fields and gathered the grapes and trodden them, they held a festival in the temple of their god. While they were eating and drinking, they cursed Abimelek.
window_text.28: Then Gaal son of Ebed said, “Who is Abimelek, and why should we Shechemites be subject to him? Isn’t he Jerub-Baal’s son, and isn’t Zebul his deputy? Serve the family of Hamor, Shechem’s father! Why should we serve Abimelek?
window_text.29: If only this people were under my command! Then I would get rid of him. I would say to Abimelek, ‘Call out your whole army!’”

question: What should Abimelek do once Gaal's force moves out to challenge him?

window_text.30: When Zebul the governor of the city heard what Gaal son of Ebed said, he was very angry.
window_text.31: Under cover he sent messengers to Abimelek, saying, “Gaal son of Ebed and his clan have come to Shechem and are stirring up the city against you.
window_text.32: Now then, during the night you and your men should come and lie in wait in the fields.
window_text.33: In the morning at sunrise, advance against the city. When Gaal and his men come out against you, seize the opportunity to attack them.”

question: Whom does Abimelek pursue to the gate?
answer: Abimelek pursues Gaal to the gate.
competitor: Abimelek pursues the citizens of Shechem to the gate.

window_text.38: Then Zebul said to him, “Where is your big talk now, you who said, ‘Who is Abimelek that we should be subject to him?’ Aren’t these the men you ridiculed? Go out and fight them!”
window_text.39: So Gaal led out the citizens of Shechem and fought Abimelek.
window_text.40: Abimelek chased him all the way to the entrance of the gate, and many were killed as they fled.
window_text.41: Then Abimelek stayed in Arumah, and Zebul drove Gaal and his clan out of Shechem.

question: What makes Abimelek rise to attack?
answer: He sees people coming out of the city.
competitor: He hears a report about people in the fields.

window_text.42: The next day the people of Shechem went out to the fields, and this was reported to Abimelek.
window_text.43: So he took his men, divided them into three companies and set an ambush in the fields. When he saw the people coming out of the city, he rose to attack them.
window_text.44: Abimelek and the companies with him rushed forward to a position at the entrance of the city gate. Then two companies attacked those in the fields and struck them down.
window_text.45: All that day Abimelek pressed his attack against the city until he had captured it and killed its people. Then he destroyed the city and scattered salt over it.

question: Who cuts branches first?
answer: Abimelek cuts branches before the men do.

window_text.46: On hearing this, the citizens in the tower of Shechem went into the stronghold of the temple of El-Berith.
window_text.47: When Abimelek heard that they had assembled there,
window_text.48: he and all his men went up Mount Zalmon. He took an ax and cut off some branches, which he lifted to his shoulders. He ordered the men with him, “Quick! Do what you have seen me do!”
window_text.49: So all the men cut branches and followed Abimelek. They piled them against the stronghold and set it on fire with the people still inside. So all the people in the tower of Shechem, about a thousand men and women, also died.

question: Why does Abimelek go to the tower entrance?

window_text.50: Next Abimelek went to Thebez and besieged it and captured it.
window_text.51: Inside the city, however, was a strong tower, to which all the men and women—all the people of the city—had fled. They had locked themselves in and climbed up on the tower roof.
window_text.52: Abimelek went to the tower and attacked it. But as he approached the entrance to the tower to set it on fire,
window_text.53: a woman dropped an upper millstone on his head and cracked his skull.

window_text.54: Hurriedly he called to his armor-bearer, “Draw your sword and kill me, so that they can’t say, ‘A woman killed him.’” So his servant ran him through, and he died.
window_text.55: When the Israelites saw that Abimelek was dead, they went home.

question: On whom does the curse fall?

window_text.56: Thus God repaid the wickedness that Abimelek had done to his father by murdering his seventy brothers.
window_text.57: God also made the people of Shechem pay for all their wickedness. The curse of Jotham son of Jerub-Baal came on them.
